process_area.title: Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns

value_stream.name: Regulatory License, Permit & Accreditation Portfolio Management

Automation Opportunity: - Renewal-package auto-assembly; dependency mapping; submission-status tracker; calendar auto-reset on receipt
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: renewal filed within lead-time; cross-domain dependencies resolved; renewed authorization recorded
Cross-references: - links to W4842/W4845/W4846 (register/calendar/evidence), VS-17 (finance), W4853 (remediation), W4854 (providers), all domain compliance VSs
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dependency-miss risk**: Renewal blocked by an unmet cross-domain dependency (e.g., expired mayor's permit blocking BIR CAS); mitigated by dependency mapping
- **Processing-delay risk**: Regulator backlog delaying renewal past expiry; mitigated by lead-time headroom + remediation (W4853)
- **Evidence-lag risk**: Renewed authorization not recorded → calendar not reset → false alert; mitigated by the update SLA
System Touchpoints: - GRC calendar/workflow (W4845); register (W4842); evidence repository (W4846); finance (VS-17); domain compliance VSs

steps.activity: On calendar alert (W4845), the domain owner prepares the renewal package (forms, supporting documents, fee) per the authorization's renewal rule and the evidence standard (W4846); coordinate any cross-domain dependencies (e.g., BIR CAS renewal needs current mayor's permit)

Submit & track: file with the regulator (or via third-party provider W4854), track processing, respond to queries, and obtain the renewed authorization within the lead-time; coordinate the fee payment (VS-17) and update the register (W4842) on receipt
Close the renewal: record renewed authorization + evidence in the repository (W4846), reset the calendar (W4845), and confirm on the dashboard; escalate any delay to remediation (W4853) before lapse

fields.Frequency: Annual per site (200 stores + 4 DCs + HQ) for LGU; periodic for BFP
fields.Owner: Compliance Operations / Store Ops (VS-07) / LGU Compliance (VS-76)
fields.Participants: Store Managers, DC Managers, Real Estate (VS-97), Finance (VS-17 fees), Third-party providers (W4854)
fields.Trigger: Annual LGU business-permit renewal season (Jan); annual BFP FSIC; recurring multi-site cycles
fields.Volume: ~205 sites × LGU business permit/mayor's permit annually; ~205 × BFP FSIC

workflows.name: Multi-Site Permit Renewal Campaigns (LGU Business Permit, Mayor's Permit, BFP FSIC)

Automation Opportunity: - Campaign-workflow with per-LGU rules; site-status tracker; package auto-distribution; coverage dashboard
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: 100% site coverage targeted; per-LGU deadlines tracked; lapses remediated; campaign results reported
Cross-references: - links to VS-76 (LGU compliance), VS-07 (store ops), VS-138 (BFP/fire), W4842/W4845 (register/calendar), W4853 (remediation), W4854 (providers)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scale risk**: 205 sites × LGU variation overwhelming execution; mitigated by campaign discipline + providers
- **Deadline-variation risk**: Different LGU deadlines causing some sites to lapse; mitigated by per-LGU sequencing
- **Store-engagement risk**: Store Managers deprioritizing permit renewal; mitigated by central support + accountability (W4844)
System Touchpoints: - GRC campaign workflow; calendar (W4845); register (W4842); store ops (VS-07); LGU compliance (VS-76); finance (VS-17)

steps.activity: Plan the annual campaign: the ~205-site LGU business-permit/mayor's-permit renewal schedule by LGU (different LGU deadlines & requirements), the BFP FSIC cycle, owners per site (Store/DC Manager + central support), the standard package, fee budget, and the third-party-provider coverage (W4854); sequence by LGU deadline
steps.r: Compliance Operations / Store Ops / LGU Compliance

steps.activity: Execute the campaign across sites: distribute packages to Store/DC Managers (or providers), track submission per site, manage LGU-specific variations (barangay clearance, sanitation, fire-safety eval), collect renewed permits, and reconcile to the calendar (W4845) and register (W4842)
Close the campaign: confirm 100% coverage, remediate any lapses (W4853), report campaign results (on-time %, lapses, cost) to governance (W4864), and capture LGU-process learnings for next year

fields.Frequency: Per new site/activity (~10–15 new stores/yr + new services/assets)
fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), Real Estate (VS-97), Government Affairs (VS-104), domain owners, providers (W4854)
fields.Trigger: New store open (VS-37); DC; off-site asset (VS-164 locker, VS-163 EV charger); new service (VS-156 VAS); remodel scope change (VS-109)
fields.Volume: ~15–25 new-site/activity acquisitions per year (10–15 new stores + remodels/DC changes)

Automation Opportunity: - Site/activity → checklist engine (W4843); parallel-acquisition tracker; go-live gate (permit-clear to open)
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: obligation-map checklist applied; authorizations obtained before go-live; recorded in register
Cross-references: - links to VS-37/109 (store lifecycle), VS-163/164 (assets), VS-156 (VAS), W4843 (obligation map), W4842/W4845/W4846 (register/calendar/evidence), W4854 (providers)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Go-live-blocking risk**: A required permit not obtained by opening day → delayed opening / illegal operation; mitigated by parallel execution and go-live gate
- **Checklist-gap risk**: A required permit omitted from the acquisition; mitigated by the obligation map (W4843)
- **Timeline-miss risk**: Regulator processing exceeding the go-live timeline; mitigated by early start + provider support
System Touchpoints: - Obligation map (W4843); store lifecycle (VS-37/109); register (W4842); calendar (W4845); government affairs (VS-104); finance (VS-17)

steps.activity: On new site/activity, generate the required-permit checklist from the obligation map (W4843) for that site type/activity/geography (LGU business permit, barangay, BFP, DENR ECC if applicable, BIR branch/CAS, sanitary, signage, occupancy, plus activity-specific e.g., BSP accreditation for VAS, NPC registration for data); sequence by the go-live timeline (VS-37)

Execute acquisition in parallel with site build/open (VS-37/VS-109): assign owners (W4844), file applications, manage LGU/regulator processing, and obtain authorizations before go-live; coordinate the fee budget (VS-17) and providers (W4854)
steps.r: Compliance Operations / Domain Owners / Providers / Real Estate

steps.activity: On receipt, load authorizations to the register (W4842), set the renewal calendar (W4845), file evidence (W4846), and confirm go-live-readiness (no activity before authorizations in place); hand off to operations (VS-07)

fields.Participants: Domain owners, Legal (VS-100.3), site managers, Internal Audit (VS-21), Records (VS-88)
fields.Trigger: Regulator inspection/audit notice (BIR, DOLE, BFP, DENR, LGU, PCAB, NPC, BSP, FDA); scheduled inspection; complaint-triggered
fields.Volume: ~150–250 inspections/audits per year across regulators and ~205 sites

workflows.name: Regulator Inspection/Audit Coordination, Calendar & Response Hub

Automation Opportunity: - Inspection-notice → evidence-packet auto-assembly; inspection calendar; corrective-action tracker; finding→risk-tier update
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: inspection response owner assigned; findings corrected & closed; outcome documented
Cross-references: - links to W4846 (evidence), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-88 (records), VS-21 (audit), W4848 (risk tiering), W4858 (penalty), W4864 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unprepared-inspection risk**: Disorganized response → escalated finding; mitigated by the evidence hub
- **Clashing-inspection risk**: Multiple regulators inspecting simultaneously; mitigated by the inspection calendar
- **Finding-cascade risk**: One finding triggering others; mitigated by coordinated corrective action
System Touchpoints: - Evidence repository (W4846); inspection calendar; legal matter (VS-100.3); records (VS-88); internal audit (VS-21); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Receive & log the inspection/audit notice, scope it (regulator, entity/site, authorization, subject), assign the response owner (W4844), and assemble the evidence packet from the repository (W4846) and records (VS-88); maintain an inspection calendar to avoid clashing inspections

steps.a: Compliance Portfolio Manager / VP Legal & Compliance
steps.activity: Host the inspection/audit, respond to findings, and coordinate corrective action across domain owners (e.g., BFP fire-safety fix via VS-138, DOLE labor via VS-19/VS-84, BIR via VS-79); manage the written response to the regulator

Track corrective-action closure, document the outcome in the audit trail (W4846), manage any penalty (W4858), and feed inspection findings to risk tiering (W4848), governance (W4864), and analytics (W4862)

fields.Owner: Compliance Portfolio Manager / Domain Owner / Legal (VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: At-risk renewal (W4845); lapsed permit; regulator notice of lapse/operating-without-permit

Automation Opportunity: - At-risk → escalation workflow; continuity-playbook trigger; root-cause tracker
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: lapse escalated immediately; continuity workaround deployed; reinstatement tracked; root-cause reviewed
Cross-references: - links to W4845 (calendar), W4849 (renewal), VS-26 (BCP), VS-100.3 (legal), W4844 (ownership), W4858 (penalty), W4862/W4864 (analytics/governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Operating-without-permit risk**: Continued operation during lapse → offense + fines + reputational harm; mitigated by continuity workaround + expedited cure
- **Store-closure risk**: A lapsed LGU/BFP permit forcing closure; mitigated by BCP workaround
- **Recurrence risk**: Same lapse recurring; mitigated by root-cause review + control strengthening
System Touchpoints: - Calendar/alerts (W4845); register (W4842); BCP (VS-26); legal (VS-100.3); finance penalty (VS-17); analytics (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~per event containment 1–5 days; reinstatement weeks; review ~2 weeks

steps.a: Compliance Portfolio Manager / VP Legal & Compliance / COO
steps.activity: Detect the lapse/at-risk (calendar alert non-response W4845, regulator notice, or self-identified); assess business impact (store-closing, bid-blocking, fines, operating-without-permit offense) and escalate to VP Legal & Compliance / COO immediately

Remediate: expedite the renewal (W4849), engage the regulator for a cure/grace period where available, and where the lapse is operational (e.g., lapsed LGU business permit) deploy the business-continuity workaround (e.g., temporary-operation permit, adjacent-site fulfillment, BCP VS-26) to sustain operations; manage any penalty (W4858)
steps.r: Domain Owner / Legal / Store Ops / BCP

steps.activity: Reinstate & prevent recurrence: obtain the renewed authorization, reset the calendar (W4845), conduct root-cause (ownership failure W4844, calendar failure, provider failure W4854), strengthen controls, and report the incident to governance (W4864) and analytics (W4862)

fields.Trigger: Permit-service need (renewal W4849, acquisition W4851, inspection W4852); provider contract; ABC/anti-corruption review

Automation Opportunity: - Provider-panel dashboard; engagement tracker; fee reconciliation; ABC-attestation workflow
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: providers DD'd (TPRM/ABC); ABC clauses in contract; deliverable verified; performance monitored
Cross-references: - links to VS-161 (TPRM), VS-86 (ABC), VS-119 (ethics), VS-91 (privacy), VS-100.3 (contract), W4849/W4851/W4852 (uses), W4853 (continuity), W4862 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **ABC/bribery risk**: A provider bribing an official on BuildRight's behalf → criminal liability (RA 3019/VS-86); mitigated by ABC clauses, due diligence, and zero-tolerance
- **Provider-failure risk**: Provider failing to obtain the permit → lapse (W4853); mitigated by panel depth + monitoring
- **Cost-leakage risk**: Over-paying providers or duplicate fees; mitigated by fee reconciliation
System Touchpoints: - Vendor master (VS-03/VS-29); TPRM (VS-161); ABC (VS-86); legal contract (VS-100.3); finance (VS-17); privacy (VS-91)
Time Estimate: - ~per onboarding 1–2 weeks DD; engagement management continuous

steps.activity: Maintain the approved permit-service-provider panel: fixers/consultants/agents by region/regulator (LGU, BFP, DENR, BIR, PCAB), with due diligence (TPRM VS-161 — financial, ABC/anti-corruption VS-86, competence, references); contract via Procurement/Legal with scope, fees, SLA, and ABC clauses

Engage per need (W4849/W4851/W4852): assign the provider, track the deliverable (permit obtained/renewed), verify authenticity, and reconcile the fee (VS-17); enforce the ABC/anti-corruption standard (no bribery of officials — links to VS-86/VS-119) and the data-privacy standard (VS-91) for any data shared

Monitor provider performance & compliance (SLA, ABC, renewals-obtained, cost), manage under-performance/failure (W4853 continuity), re-compete, and feed provider record to TPRM (VS-161) and analytics (W4862); report provider-related ABC risk to governance (W4864)

fields.Participants: Domain owners, Government Affairs (VS-104), Real Estate (VS-97), Legal (VS-100.3)
fields.Trigger: Permits requiring multi-regulator sign-off (e.g., new store needs LGU + BFP + DENR + BIR); concurrent renewal cycles; conflicting regulator requirements
fields.Volume: ~10–15 multi-permit acquisitions per year (one per new store) plus renewal campaigns

Automation Opportunity: - Multi-permit dependency-graph engine; critical-path tracker; inter-agency-process library
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: dependency graph followed; conflicts escalated via Government Affairs/Legal; bundle tracked to completion
Cross-references: - links to W4843 (obligation map), W4842 (register), VS-104 (government affairs), VS-100.3 (legal), W4849/W4851 (acquisition/renewal), W4862 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dependency-bottleneck risk**: A slow regulator blocking downstream permits; mitigated by dependency mapping + Government Affairs
- **Conflict risk**: Conflicting regulator requirements (e.g., BFP vs DENR on a site); mitigated by Legal/Government Affairs resolution
- **Sequencing-error risk**: Filing out of sequence → rejection; mitigated by the dependency graph
System Touchpoints: - Obligation map (W4843); register (W4842); government affairs (VS-104); legal (VS-100.3); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Map the multi-permit dependency graph for the need (e.g., a new store: SEC/DTI → LGU business permit needs BFP FSIC + barangay clearance + DENR ECC + sanitary; BIR branch needs LGU permit); identify the critical path and sequencing constraints

Coordinate concurrent renewals/acquisitions across regulators: sequence filings, manage cross-regulator dependencies (permit B needs permit A), resolve conflicting requirements, and leverage Government Affairs (VS-104) relationships to smooth bottlenecks
steps.r: Compliance Operations / Domain Owners / Government Affairs

steps.activity: Track the multi-permit bundle to completion, update the register (W4842), and capture inter-agency-process learnings (e.g., a region where DENR-BFP sequencing is slow) for the obligation map (W4843) and analytics (W4862)

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), Real Estate (VS-97), Legal (VS-100.3), Government Affairs (VS-104)
fields.Trigger: Business/activity change (scope expansion, new product line, signage change, floor-area change); site transfer/closure (VS-59); entity restructuring

workflows.name: Permit Variation, Scope Change & Site-Transfer/Closure Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Change-trigger detection from store/real-estate events; variation-checklist engine; closure-permit-surrender checklist
Controls: - CTL-729 (ensure controlled execution — Renewal Execution, Inspection Coordination & Multi-Site Campaigns (PA-166.2).)
- CTL-729: change-triggers assessed for permit impact; variations approved before changed activity; closure permits surrendered
Cross-references: - links to VS-59 (store closure), VS-97 (real estate), VS-07 (store ops), W4843 (obligation map), W4842/W4845/W4846 (register/calendar/evidence), W4862 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unreported-change risk**: A scope/area change not triggering a permit variation → non-compliance; mitigated by change-trigger detection (links to store ops/real estate)
- **Closure-orphan risk**: Permits not surrendered on site closure → stale records/fees; mitigated by closure checklist
- **Timeline risk**: Changed activity starting before the variation is approved; mitigated by a pre-activity gate
System Touchpoints: - Obligation map (W4843); register (W4842); calendar (W4845); store closure (VS-59); real estate (VS-97); legal (VS-100.3)

steps.activity: Detect the change-trigger (scope/activity/scope/signage/area change, store closure VS-59, transfer, entity restructuring) and assess permit impact from the obligation map (W4843): which authorizations need variation/amendment/surrender/new-application
steps.r: Regulatory Intelligence / Compliance Operations / Domain Owner

steps.a: Compliance Portfolio Manager / VP Legal & Compliance
steps.activity: Execute the variation: file amendments with the relevant regulators (e.g., expanded floor area → amended building/occupancy permit + BFP re-eval; new product line → DTI-BPS/DENR if regulated), obtain approvals before the changed activity, and surrender/cancel permits on site closure (VS-59)

Update the register (W4842), evidence (W4846), and calendar (W4845); confirm no orphaned/invalid permits remain after closure/transfer; feed variation-volume and closure-compliance to analytics (W4862) and governance (W4864)
